title: Bijective open pullback Hom restriction on supported tests
statement: Let $s:Y\to S$ be a morphism of schemes, $B\subset Y$ an open, and assume derived categories of sheaves of modules in the common Hom universe $w$ on every scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-derived-category]. Put $L=\operatorname{schemeMVDerivedRestriction}(Y,B)$ [def-pc-derived-mayer-vietoris-canonical-data]. Supply an adjunction $a:LB.\iota^*\dashv RB.\iota_*$ [def-pc-derived-pullback, lem-pc-perfect-hom-transport]. For $r:T\to S$, put $\pi_r:Y\times_S T\to Y$, $\pi'_r:B\times_S T\to B$, and let $b_r:B\times_S T\to Y\times_S T$ be the pullback map induced by $B.\iota$ and the identities. Thus $b_r\pi_r=\pi'_r B.\iota$. Let $\sigma:L\cong LB.\iota^*$ be the mate of the identity on the common right adjoint between $a$ and $\operatorname{schemeMVAdjunction}(Y,B)$. Define $\kappa_r:L\pi_r^*;Lb_r^*\cong L;L\pi_r'^*$ as $c(b_r,\pi_r)$, then the equality comparison of the preceding cartesian equality, then $c(\pi'_r,B.\iota)^{-1}$, then $\sigma^{-1}$ whiskered by $L\pi_r'^*$, where $c$ is the fixed counit-pinned perfectHomComposition [lem-pc-perfect-hom-transport]. For derived objects $M,Q$ on $Y$ and $f:L\pi_r^*M\to L\pi_r^*Q$, put $\tau_r(f)=\kappa_r(M)^{-1};Lb_r^*(f);\kappa_r(Q)$. If $L:\operatorname{Hom}(M,E)\to\operatorname{Hom}(LM,LE)$ is bijective for every derived object $E$ on $Y$, then $\tau_r:\operatorname{Hom}(L\pi_r^*M,L\pi_r^*Q)\to\operatorname{Hom}(L\pi_r'^*LM,L\pi_r'^*LQ)$ is bijective. The Lean interface allows a supplied comparison equal to this explicitly defined $\kappa_r$, to avoid unfolding its construction in downstream proofs.

proof.text: Using the exact extension-by-zero adjunction, identify the all-target Hom bijectivity hypothesis with invertibility of the counit J(LM) -> M by the Hom adjunction and Yoneda. Thus M is the supported extension of LM.

Compute pullback using a K-flat representative. On each stalk, tensor pullback of extension by zero agrees with extension by zero along the inverse-image open: inside the open it is the same stalk tensor, and outside it is zero. This constructs the derived cartesian extension-by-zero comparison. Identify the inverse-image open with B x_S T by the canonical pullback lifts.

The derived extension/restriction adjunction gives bijectivity on Hom out of the supported pullback. The canonical composition and open-adjunction mate comparisons identify this function with tau_r. Substitute the supplied comparison equation and conjugate by kappa_r; conjugation by isomorphisms preserves bijectivity.

lean.statement:
theorem perfect_hom_open_test_bijective
    {S Y T : Scheme.{u}} (s : Y ⟶ S) (B : Y.Opens) (r : T ⟶ S)
    [∀ Z : Scheme.{u}, HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Z.toRingedSpace))]
    (a : derivedPullback B.ι ⊣ schemeDerivedDirectImage B.ι)
    (M Q : schemeDerivedCategory Y)
    (hM : ∀ E : schemeDerivedCategory Y,
      Function.Bijective (fun f : M ⟶ E ↦ (schemeMVDerivedRestriction Y B).map f)) :
    let b := pullback.map (B.ι ≫ s) r s r B.ι (𝟙 T) (𝟙 S) (by simp) (by simp)
    let σ : schemeMVDerivedRestriction Y B ≅ derivedPullback B.ι :=
      (conjugateIsoEquiv a (schemeMVAdjunction Y B)).symm (Iso.refl _)
    let he : b ≫ pullback.fst s r = pullback.fst (B.ι ≫ s) r ≫ B.ι := by
      simp [b, pullback.map]
    let κ₀ := perfectHomComposition b (pullback.fst s r) ≪≫
      eqToIso (congrArg (fun f ↦ derivedPullback f) he) ≪≫
      (perfectHomComposition (pullback.fst (B.ι ≫ s) r) B.ι).symm ≪≫
      Functor.isoWhiskerRight σ.symm (derivedPullback (pullback.fst (B.ι ≫ s) r))
    ∀ κ : derivedPullback (pullback.fst s r) ⋙ derivedPullback b ≅
        schemeMVDerivedRestriction Y B ⋙ derivedPullback (pullback.fst (B.ι ≫ s) r),
      κ = κ₀ →
    Function.Bijective (fun f : (derivedPullback (pullback.fst s r)).obj M ⟶
        (derivedPullback (pullback.fst s r)).obj Q ↦
      κ.inv.app M ≫ (derivedPullback b).map f ≫ κ.hom.app Q)
